narrativeContract.foundation: Nebraska's origins, Bob Devaney, Tom Osborne and the system that earned five national championships
narrativeContract.conflict: The long post-Osborne decline, questions of program leadership and adaptation, multiple distinctive eras, and lost national stature
narrativeContract.resolution: Evidence of rebuilding under Matt Rhule and what remains unsettled in 2026. Program future is not predetermined.
truthRules: No invented game footage, coach speech, fan quotes, player action or period audio
Historical facts from original records; competing decline hypotheses require independently attributed evidence
Bo Pelini's repeated nine-win seasons may not be mislabeled losing seasons or equal to Riley/Frost results
Do not claim conference changes, staff dismissals, recruiting or coach motives singly caused a complex decline without analysis
Early 1900s footage may be approximately dated; no false exact attribution
Distinguish 2024 real bowl progress and 2025 7–6 from 2026 5–2 and late-game failures
Episode 3 finale is contingent on real October/November and postseason outcomes
Do not auto-synthesize interviews, archival crowd sound or alleged broadcasts
No publication without independently reviewed footage rights, signed participant releases and founder approval

workingFilmReferences.note: Reclassify from Ep02 to Ep03. Existing test and real-play requirement still applies.

episodes.title: The Giant
episodes.question: How did Nebraska become one of college football's most formidable programs?
episodes.editorialObjective: Go from origins to the five titles, reveal the institutional football model and emotional identity that made Nebraska a giant, ending on the height of that expectation.

acts.storyQuestion: What did winning a national championship actually mean to the state, and why did it seem repeatable?
Who built Nebraska football before anybody called it a dynasty?
What changed after Bob Devaney arrived in 1962?
What happened in 1970 and 1971, and how did those teams prove sustained dominance was possible?
How did the walk-on system, player development, Blackshirts, recruiting and coaching continuity work together?
What did the 1994, 1995 and 1997 championships create for everyone who came next?

episodes.audienceValue: Go from origins to the five titles, reveal the institutional football model and emotional identity that made Nebraska a giant, ending on the height of that expectation.

episodes.title: The Sleeping Giant
episodes.question: How did a perennial national power lose its place, and what actually went wrong?
episodes.editorialObjective: Investigate turning points and structural explanations fairly, separating 2000s shocks, Pelini-era nine-win consistency, institutional decisions and the much deeper later losing stretch.

acts.storyQuestion: Was the 2001 Colorado loss a turning point or a warning sign of changes already happening?
How did 2002 and Solich's dismissal after the 2003 regular season change the program's trajectory?
How did Callahan's replacement of core football systems play out, and which criticisms survive the evidence?
Why was Pelini's consistent nine-win era still viewed as falling short, and how did the 2011 Big Ten move change expectations?
How did the Riley and Frost eras differ and why did Nebraska go so long without a bowl appearance?
Were the roots coaching turnover, talent, leadership, development, conference demands, or a changing sport? What evidence would distinguish them?

episodes.audienceValue: Investigate turning points and structural explanations fairly, separating 2000s shocks, Pelini-era nine-win consistency, institutional decisions and the much deeper later losing stretch.

episodes.title: The Giant Stirs
episodes.question: What has Nebraska genuinely rebuilt under Matt Rhule, and how far is it from national relevance?
episodes.editorialObjective: Show changes in staffing, culture, player development and documented outcomes; admit both the bowl milestone and frustrating 2026 finishes, leaving the program's future open.

acts.storyQuestion: What was Nebraska's actual condition when Rhule took over in 2023?
What has changed in recruiting, veteran roster development, facilities, coaching, training and accountability, and can we see it?
What did the 2024 Pinstripe Bowl breakthrough and the 2025 7-6 record mean, and what limitations remained?
What did five straight wins show, and what did the two losses to Indiana and Oregon reveal about finishing?
How do Nebraska's Washington and remaining 2026 games change the evidence without a scripted winning streak?
What can we honestly conclude once the season ends, and how do former and younger supporters see Nebraska's next chapter?

episodes.audienceValue: Show changes in staffing, culture, player development and documented outcomes; admit both the bowl milestone and frustrating 2026 finishes, leaving the program's future open.

releasePolicy.ep1: No release until factual historical archive, old game footage, voices and rights independently verified and film creatively approved
releasePolicy.ep2: No single-cause blame narrative or made-up former coach testimony; history rights and primary-source attribution required
releasePolicy.ep3: Future games must be played and checked; no imagined comeback, forecast ending or unlicensed 2026 broadcast visuals
